name: AI Ecosystem Focus Group
summary: The field of scientific AI/ML has evolved rapidly in recent years. As AI/ML implementations are applied to complex life science challenges, common issues have emerged, such as the output of poorly des
body:
The field of scientific AI/ML has evolved rapidly in recent years. As AI/ML implementations are applied to complex life science challenges, common issues have emerged, such as the output of poorly described AI datasets and models that commonly do not follow best practices. This has created fundamental problems with reproducibility, explainability, and trustworthiness, limiting the value of published AI datasets and models for the wider scientific community. In response, a diverse range of new AI/ML standards, metadata schemas, and AI-focused resources such as registries have been developed. However, these efforts have led to fragmentation and poor interoperability between AI/ML support infrastructure both within and outside of ELIXIR, creating a new set of challenges for building a harmonised ecosystem of impactful and reusable AI/ML research outputs.

The AI Ecosystem Focus Group brings together experts from ELIXIR’s Nodes  to address growing challenges within the scientific AI/ML field, particularly  the need for harmonisation in AI/ML infrastructure. Building on the foundational work of the ELIXIR Machine Learning Focus Group, the AI Ecosystem Focus Group's main purpose is to coordinate efforts, address fragmentation, and support the standardisation of AI/ML infrastructure, ultimately aiming to build a more impactful and reusable ecosystem for AI/ML research outputs across ELIXIR.

name: BioinfoCoreLeaders Club
summary: A UK community for leaders and managers of bioinformatics, computational biology and related core shared research facilities. Launched in 2026, it convened a national forum for people who lead, manage
body:
A UK community for leaders and managers of bioinformatics, computational biology and related core shared research facilities.  

Launched in 2026, it convened a national forum for people who lead, manage or strategically support bioinformatics, computational biology, data science and related research service facilities in UK universities and not-for-profit research institutes.

Open to all, the community exists to cut duplicated effort, share operational and strategic practice, and give facility leaders a route into national discussions about research infrastructure, workforce sustainability and the responsible use of AI. 

It grew out of an informal network of facility leaders and was formalised as an ELIXIR-UK community  through the Flexible Bursaries Scheme activity BioinfoCore Connect UK. Seventeen organisations took part in the first meeting at the University of Liverpool in May 2026, A short story of the BioinfoCoreLeaders Club.

Recurring topics include cost recovery and pricing, service governance, procurement, demand against capacity, and career pathways and recognition for digital Research Technical Professionals (dRTPs). Longer term the community intends to produce good-practice resources, position statements, consultation responses and shared recommendations for funders and institutions.

What to expect

Compare costing and service models

Discuss pricing, cost recovery, procurement and the gap between demand and capacity with people running comparable facilities. Find out what others charge, what they refuse and how they justify it.

Borrow rather than build

Share templates, standard operating procedures, costing models, training approaches and examples of service governance, so each facility stops solving the same problem alone.

Strengthen FAIR and reproducible research

Compare how facilities handle metadata, workflows, repositories, code sharing and data stewardship in a service setting, where reproducibility depends on work you do not own.

Talk frankly with peers

Meet others carrying the same responsibilities for facility strategy, operations and staffing. Raise the problems that are difficult to discuss inside your own institution, in a trusted and informal setting.

Shape national conversations

Contribute evidence and expertise to discussions about service provision, FAIR practice, AI adoption, research integrity and sustainable infrastructure, through consultation responses and position statements.

Connect to national infrastructure

Build direct links between your facility and ELIXIR-UK and other national research infrastructure initiatives, and identify collaborators for joint resources and grant applications.

Who is this for

The community is open to all. It is aimed at people responsible for facility strategy, operations or service delivery in UK higher education and not-for-profit research organisations, including:

  • Heads and directors of bioinformatics, computational biology and related core facilities
  • Facility managers and principal dRTPs
  • People with an active interest in the leadership and strategic development of research service facilities

Wider facility staff are welcome and can contribute through community activities and events, including bioinformaticians, data scientists, research software engineers, statisticians, data stewards, trainers and early-career dRTPs.

Initial topic leads

Four priority themes were identified at the inaugural meeting, with leads volunteering to take each forward.

  • FAIR and reproducible practice: Robert Andrews, Sam Haynes and Nicholas Owen
  • Advocacy: Lauren Mee
  • Peer-community support: Leo Zeef and Matthieu Miossec
  • Network promotion: Sascha Ott

FAQs

Is there a cost to join?

No. Membership is free. ELIXIR-UK support gives the community a maintained digital platform at no cost to members, and the co-chairs are seeking further funding to widen access to in-person events.

What commitment is expected?

The community aims to meet monthly online. Members are encouraged to attend where they can and to share practice or evidence with the wider community. The model is deliberately light-touch while the network matures.

Which organisations are involved?

17 organisations took part in the inaugural activity, spanning universities, research institutes and CRUK institutes, with further representation added since. See how the community formed for the full list.

name: Cancer Data Community
summary: Cancer research is highly data intensive, making efficient data management essential to enabling precision medicine for European citizens. The ELIXIR Cancer Data Community was established early in 202
body:
Cancer research is highly data intensive, making efficient data management essential to enabling precision medicine for European citizens.

The ELIXIR Cancer Data Community was established early in 2024, following the publication of the Community’s white paper. The Community brings together expertise and resources to gather, manage and analyse clinical and biomedical data. By joining forces with other initiatives focused on human data, including several Horizon Europe-funded projects, ELIXIR aims to enhance the data infrastructure, improving the accessibility, quality and interoperability of data, ultimately accelerating discoveries in biomedical research and enabling better decision-making.

Effective data management involves the adoption of standardised data formats, robust data privacy and the engagement of healthcare professionals. Broad interoperability of data, metadata, research software and computational infrastructure are all critical for data to make a difference to cancer prevention and treatment.

The scope of the Community includes running pilot projects, delivering training and lectures, providing a network of experts to respond to funding opportunities, and influencing the direction of policy development in cancer research.

name: Credit, Recognition and Usage Focus Group
summary: Modern life science research relies on contributions beyond traditional publications – software, workflows, datasets, training materials and the people who develop, curate, coordinate and maintain res
body:
Modern life science research relies on contributions beyond traditional publications – software, workflows, datasets, training materials and the people who develop, curate, coordinate and maintain research infrastructure. These are often not adequately recognised by existing research evaluation systems.

The Credit, Recognition and Usage Focus Group connects experts from ELIXIR Nodes, Platforms and Communities to coordinate ELIXIR-wide activities on credit, recognition and usage, align approaches and avoid duplication of effort. Its expected activities include mapping contribution and usage types across ELIXIR, developing best practice recommendations and supporting ELIXIR-led services such as APICURON and BIP! Scholar. The group also engages with external infrastructures such as OpenAIRE and ORCID.

name: Data Stewardship Training Fellowship
summary: Professionalising data stewardship in the life sciences With a Fellowship of ambassadors across UK research-performing organisations Through UKRI funding gained in 2021, we have established a national
body:
Professionalising data stewardship in the life sciences

With a Fellowship of ambassadors across UK research-performing organisations

Through UKRI funding gained in 2021, we have established a national Data Stewardship Fellowship in a seedcorn group of 17 UK universities and institutes.

Fellows have been supported in creating learning materials and offering local training in their fields of FAIR data expertise by leveraging existing resources, materials and contact points within their institutions.

These activities have supported a short-term mission to develop a sustainable data skills training programme in the Life Sciences, realised through embedding material locally into existing in-house training programmes and research infrastructure.

Learn more about the activities

You can find all the activities Fellows have been involved in by visiting the dedicated microsite.

Visit fellowship site

This Fellowship now front-loads a longer-term vision to grow a FAIR data community and national capacity in Data Stewardship. Through mobilising ELIXIR communities, services and platforms, we aim to support Fellows and UK Data Stewards in becoming FAIR data ambassadors within a network of peers and mentors.

This community aims to:

  • Support professionalising data stewardship in the life sciences
  • Develop resources to help researchers make their data FAIR
  • Upskill life sciences professionals about the importance of making their data FAIR
  • Work with publishers to make sure that data is published in a FAIR way

What's new

Meet our Fellows

The community’s landscape

Expanding our reach beyond the ELIXIR-UK Network 

We have embedded the Fellowship programme within the broader ELIXIR-UK strategy, granting Fellows long-term support for their work with a national and international outlook.

Through UKRI funding gained in 2021, the Fellowship has founded a network of Data Stewards in a seedcorn group of UK research-performing organisations. A cohort of 24 Fellows across 17 organisations,  spanning diverse bioscience disciplines, have mobilised their Research Data Management colleagues in libraries and research offices.

Fellows come from both ELIXIR-UK members and other UK research-performing organisations, expanding the reach of our network and mission. As a result, some Fellows have spearheaded their organisations' applications to join the UK Node.

Embedding Fellows into the Node’s core activities

Within the ELIXIR-UK community, dedicated RDM and training working groups facilitate cross-disciplinary cooperation. These groups hold monthly meetings, which also include the active participation of the Fellows.

UK RDM Club
UK Training Club

Opening up Fellows to the wider ELIXIR Europe network

Such groups are also connected to the pan-European ELIXIR Communities, including the recently established Research Data Management Community and the ELIXIR Training Platform.  Members of the fellowship coordination team lead many of these activities. 

Partnering with other initiatives and ELIXIR members

In addition, we are working with the ELIXIR Netherlands and Luxembourg Nodes to build their national data stewardship fellowship based on our success.

Our partnership with the Software Sustainability Institute (SSI) and the Galaxy Training Network, further provide us with valuable expertise in building communities of practice and fellowship programmes. 

The community’s operational essentials

A support system: the coordination team

Our Fellows have continuous support from a dedicated coordination team, creating a sense of belonging within the ELIXIR-UK initiative. This support extends to:

  • Diverse communication channels: A variety of active communication channels, including Slack, emails and online/face-to-face meetings, facilitate knowledge sharing not only related to the Fellowship outputs but also support Fellows in their daily work and career growth.
  • Regular troubleshooting sessions: several monthly drop-in sessions to troubleshoot issues, address common challenges and exchange valuable insights have kept the Fellows supported and connected. 
  • Community engagement: Monthly or bi-monthly community calls and yearly in-person retreats have given a space to discuss relevant topics with speakers that introduce valuable tools, resources and initiatives. Fellows have used this space to showcase progress, inspire others, solicit constructive feedback, and shape the Fellowship's activities.
  • Onboarding process and community intranet: documenting and ensuring all community members have the required information is crucial to our success. For instance, all Fellows attend an inaugural meeting, complete the ELIXIR Train-the-Trainer and have access to a centralised intranet with guides, templates and resources. 

“The organisation, dedication and enthusiasm of staff has been exceptional and inspirational.”

“I loved the supportive and positive environment.”

“The Train the Trainer course at the start has been incredibly useful. This was my first time attending a course of such a kind, and it will reshape how I teach. Thank you.”

Compensation and recognition

Recognising and compensating the contributions of our Fellows and Mentors is a central pillar of this initiative. Fellows receive an honorarium for the time invested in the activities within this Fellowship. 

While financial compensation is not the primary motivation for our Fellows, we strongly believe in professionalising data stewardship as an essential component of research. This goes beyond being an afterthought or an additional burden on researchers’ daily responsibilities and into an enticing career path that supports their work. 

A badge of recognition as ELIXIR-UK Fellows

While we welcome professionals who work with data in the life sciences at any career stage, a panel of experts scrutinises applications.

All candidates must not only demonstrate a strong understanding of data management in their fields but also have excellent communication and teamwork skills. Only some can pass this thorough selection process, not only guaranteeing excellence but also providing our Fellows with a badge of recognition for their skills and experience. 

Several Fellows have attested to the amplified impact of their voices in advocating for data management best practices in their organisations after becoming ELIXIR-UK Fellows. After being selected, they had a stronger voice in meetings, a motto we have adopted in our outreach: “Trust me, I’m an ELIXIR-UK Fellow.”

“As a Fellow, I gained influencing power at my institute for RDM. It gave me more authority. I’m no longer a single voice saying we should care about RDM. Instead, I have the ELIXIR-UK community behind me. Don’t underestimate that value!”

name: Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Focus Group
summary: A diverse community does not automatically provide equal opportunities for everyone to participate, contribute or progress. Previous initiatives, including ELEAD and ELIXIR-STEERS, have generated insi
body:
A diverse community does not automatically provide equal opportunities for everyone to participate, contribute or progress. Previous initiatives, including ELEAD and ELIXIR-STEERS, have generated insights and examples of good practice, but there is currently no network-wide structure to coordinate, sustain and monitor equity, diversity and inclusion across ELIXIR.

The Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Focus Group brings together expertise from across ELIXIR to coordinate existing efforts and support implementation of the ELIXIR Equal Opportunity Strategy. Initial activities include a baseline assessment of EDI-related practices, needs and priorities across ELIXIR Nodes, guidance for inclusive and accessible events and for newcomer integration, and a practical toolkit of EDI resources for use across ELIXIR.

summary: Establishing the basis for a distributed and interoperable network of regional and national pathogen data hubs. Goals Through a joint effort, the Focus Group will work towards: Establishing consensus
body:
Establishing the basis for a distributed and interoperable network of regional and national pathogen data hubs.

Goals

Through a joint effort, the Focus Group will work towards:

  • Establishing consensus and promoting the use and reuse of data, metadata and analysis standards
  • Promoting FAIR data sharing and equity
  • Proposing benchmark datasets and quality assessments
  • Fostering capacity building for pandemic preparedness through training, maturity models and tools
  • Liaising with global pathogen epidemiology initiatives (e.g. PHA4GE, WHO, ECDC)

The Focus Group will invite experts and stakeholders to join in this concerted, expert-driven effort towards sustaining and ensuring high-quality data for global surveillance and research.

name: RNA Data Focus Group
summary: Long-read sequencing and methods capable of detecting RNA modifications are transforming how RNA data are generated, processed and interpreted. However, the pace of technological innovation has outstr
body:
Long-read sequencing and methods capable of detecting RNA modifications are transforming how RNA data are generated, processed and interpreted. However, the pace of technological innovation has outstripped the development of shared standards, benchmarks and best practices.

The RNA Data Focus Group brings together experts from across ELIXIR to address these challenges. It aims to develop common standards for new-generation RNA sequencing data, establish continuous benchmarking activities and track emerging technologies through coordinated ‘technology watch’ efforts. The group develops benchmarking projects for long-read transcriptomics, building on activities launched at BioHackathon Europe 2025 in Berlin, and meets every fourth Thursday of the month.

body:
Connecting UK human data research infrastructure

Launched in 2023, the Human Data and Tech Club connects the UK human data research infrastructure and technology communities with ELIXIR and other European initiatives. It enables shared solutions, open science and impactful collaboration in health and human data research.

This community, jointly convened by ELIXIR-UK and HDR UK, provides a space for connection and exchange on human and health data research infrastructure and technology in the UK and remains open to all.

It brings together ELIXIR-UK’s experience in life science data infrastructure with perspectives from HDR UK and DARE UK’s health and human data research community and technical innovation.

What to expect

Discover tools, services and infrastructure

Learn about UK and European human data tools, platforms and services that support secure, FAIR and responsible research — including resources developed through ELIXIR, HDR UK and related initiatives.

Connect UK work to European initiatives and beyond

Hear about ongoing European human data activities and infrastructure through ELIXIR, and explore how UK teams can engage, contribute or align with work happening beyond the UK.

Share practice and build connections

Meet others working with human data across research, infrastructure and technology roles. Exchange ideas, compare approaches and discuss shared challenges in a trusted, informal setting.

Influence open and interoperable development

Provide input into human data technology development, helping to shape open practices, standards and interoperable solutions that support the wider research ecosystem.

Contribute to projects and funding opportunities

Identify opportunities to contribute to HDR UK, ELIXIR and European ongoing projects and new grant applications in the context of this community – including chances to shape ideas early and connect with potential collaborators.

Who is this for

This community is for anyone interested in human data in the life sciences at all career stages, whether within ELIXIR-UK or outside. This includes, but is not limited to:

  • Technical staff (e.g. data stewards, data custodians, bioinformaticians, software engineers)
  • Methodologists (e.g. statisticians, epidemiologists)
  • Students of human data subjects in the life sciences
  • Researchers
  • Trainers and educators
  • Health professionals (e.g. clinicians, nurses, allied health professionals)
  • Research support teams

body:
Launched in October 2020, this club focuses on ELIXIR-UK activities that help people manage their life science research data.

Who is this for

We welcome participation from data stewards, support staff and researchers interested in Research Data Management (RDM) in the life sciences.

What to expect

We meet over Zoom on the first Tuesday of every month (excluding July, August and January).  These regular meetings focus on sharing experiences and signposting new projects, resources, communities and training. This club also forms contact points for a growing pan-European network of data expertise within ELIXIR.

How to get involved

If you wish to be involved in the group, please sign up using our Join in button.  You will start receiving all our calendar invites and relevant information.  We’re open to everyone.

body:
Launched in October 2020, the ELIXIR-UK Training Club aims to support training in ELIXIR-UK member organisations.

The Group actively searches for funding opportunities and promotes diversity and inclusion of training activities, ensuring that all UK member organisations have training support.

It holds regular meetings focusing on performing/appraising training work.

The current audience, although not exclusively, is the life science researcher, and the output from the group should be useful for early career researchers. This will broaden as the group grows into supporting participants engaged in infrastructure and tool development.
